$comment: What lies between the two faces (docs/BIFACIAL_WORLD.md §2, §6; owner 2026-10-21: "add bedrock back in between the two faces … the portals are holes through the bedrock leading up to the surface on both sides"). `bedrock`: the block generated in the cells either side of the midplane, `thickness` metres on each face (a whole number of cells, inside the core). `portals`: a few vertical shafts per world, sited from the seed alone (crates/dwell-worldgen/src/portals.rs): `count` [min, max] of them (the seed picks the number), at least `spacing` m apart, within `within` m of the disc's centre, tried at up to `attempts` seeded points; a site needs land on both faces over its whole footprint, at least `inland` m from both coasts, its ground on both faces at most `maxHeight` m above sea level (the shaft is then at most 2 × (sea level + maxHeight) m long). The shaft is round, `radius` m (column centres within it are open from each face's ground to the midplane, the bedrock and core included); its opening is ringed `rim.width` m wide by `rim.height` m of `rim.block` over the ground; `ladder.block` runs the shaft's whole length on its `ladder.wall` side (north, east, south or west: the wall the ladder is fixed to), continuous across the midplane; no tree or decoration stands within `clear` m of the rim; `motes` names the look of the glowing motes drawn in the shaft round the midplane (shared/look/motes.json; a client look, not terrain). Prototype content (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.1). Changing any value changes the terrain a seed generates: regenerate the goldens (`cargo run -p dwell-worldgen --example goldens`) and ship it on a new compatibility line. Run `node shared/worldgen/gen.mjs` after editing; CI fails on stale output.
